purpose: Stage 8/E deliverable (narrow evidence/curriculum-modelling/validation correction pass, 2026-09-06): a diagnostic, read-only, MULTI-AXIS mapping of all 133 governed Unit 202 learning points against the pre-existing, independently-authored learner-facing runtime corpus. Schema v2 replaces the prior single-category-per-LP model (v1, superseded) with independent axes, since an LP can have multiple simultaneous deficits a single category collapses. The governed curriculum is the source of truth throughout; the runtime corpus is evaluated against it, never the reverse. No lesson, storyboard, assertion, or question was re-authored in producing this mapping.
method: Six independent research agents, one per batch, each read every learning point in that batch's LEARNING-POINTS.json in full and searched the live runtime corpus (scripts/content/data/*.ts, apps/mobile/src/lib/proving-content, apps/mobile/src/components/diagrams, reports/instructional-visuals/semantic-audit.json and premium-artwork/proof/) for matching, missing, wrong-depth, obsolete, or unvisualised content.

axisDefinitions.lessonCoverageStatus: NOT_TAUGHT | TAUGHT_PARTIAL | TAUGHT_CORRECT | TAUGHT_AS_SETTLED_FACT (taught with more confidence/finality than the governed evidence itself currently supports) | UNKNOWN
axisDefinitions.depthStatus: N/A | TOO_SHALLOW | CORRECT_DEPTH | TOO_DEEP_SCOPE_CREEP (teaches/assesses beyond what the governed LP requires or explicitly excludes)
axisDefinitions.assessmentCoverageStatus: NOT_ASSESSED | PARTIALLY_ASSESSED | FULLY_ASSESSED | CORRECTLY_NOT_ASSESSED (context-only/retired, correctly unassessed) | UNKNOWN
axisDefinitions.visualCoverageStatus: NOT_APPLICABLE | MISSING | PRODUCED_NOT_WIRED (asset exists in production-proof storage but not in the shipped app) | PRESENT_UNVERIFIED (asset exists but drawn with more confidence than governed evidence supports) | PRESENT_VERIFIED (passes semantic-audit contract)
axisDefinitions.obsoleteContentFlag: true if the runtime teaches/assesses something the governed curriculum has explicitly retired, corrected, or found unsupported
axisDefinitions.curriculumDispositionState: the governed LP's CURRENT LIVE evidenceReadiness (READY | HELD_PENDING_EVIDENCE_CORRECTION | DEFERRED_CONTEXT_ONLY | RETIRED_OUT_OF_SCOPE), refreshed as of this pass's final state -- not a frozen snapshot
axisDefinitions.contentAheadOfEvidenceRisk: true if the runtime teaches/assesses this LP's content as settled fact while its governed evidenceReadiness is HELD_PENDING_EVIDENCE_CORRECTION (validator check 57 enforces this is never left unflagged)
axisDefinitions.urgencySafetyImpact: NONE | LOW | MEDIUM | HIGH -- HIGH is reserved for live, actively-assessed, obsolete/retired-claim content (a learner could be certified on a specific claim the qualification's own evidence review rejected)

SCOPE-CREEP NOTE (not a factual error): the runtime teaches Faraday's law quantitatively as an assessed calculation (formula.flux_change_emf, e=N.dPhi/dt), which EMI-LP-14's own explicitData explicitExclusions rule out as not required at this level. Should be reconciled (confirmed as belonging to a different/later governed unit) rather than left as an undocumented mismatch.

EL-APPLICATION-SECURITY-ALARM-TRANSISTOR-THYRISTOR-001 (cc04-unit202-electrical-science.ts) teaches, as REQUIRED_FOR fact, and actively assesses (question text: "...which component latches on and continues to power the sounder even if the loop is reclosed...") the exact NC-loop-reclose-survival claim, sourced to ElProCus, a hobbyist tutorial site outside any permitted authority class. [Section F, third narrow correction pass] The general SCR-latches-and-keeps-a-sounder-energised relationship is now independently VERIFIED via PA-UNIT202-20260906-SCR-ALARM-EXEMPLAR-001 (Ray Marston/Nuts & Volts) -- but the runtime's specific "survives loop reclose" behaviour is a different, more specific claim tied to the still-retired NC-loop topology, and remains unevidenced. The runtime question should be revised to test the general (now-evidenced) relationship, not the loop-reclose-specific detail.

EL-APPLICATION-TELEPHONE-MASTER-SOCKET-001 (cc04-unit202-electrical-science.ts) teaches and assesses the capacitor DC-block/AC-pass ringer function and the resistor line-test function as REQUIRED_FOR fact, sourced to Wikipedia. NOTE: the capacitor-function claim is now independently confirmed by this pass's own governed evidence acquisition (SIN 351 + IXYS/Littelfuse AN-144), so it is no longer content-ahead-of-evidence for that specific facet as of this pass's correction -- but the runtime's own citation (Wikipedia) remains an unpermitted-class source, and the resistor line-test claim and the "extension sockets contain none of these components" claim both remain genuinely unevidenced and should still be corrected/re-sourced or removed at the runtime-content level.

contentAheadOfEvidenceRows.note: [Section H, third narrow correction pass] The deterministic component-symbols renderer draws a definite LED symbol and inverter block with no caveat to the learner, though the governed EDA-LP-16 explicitly holds both symbols' geometry as unverified against the current IEC 60617 standard (see its own evidenceReadinessNote/gaps). This is a genuine content-ahead-of-evidence case, not merely a missing-visual gap -- correcting the prior mis-classification as visualCoverageStatus=NOT_APPLICABLE and contentAheadOfEvidenceRisk=false, which incorrectly implied no visual exists and no risk arises, when in fact a visual exists and asserts more certainty than the governed evidence supports.

SAFETY FINDING (narrowed, not resolved): a live, actively-assessed runtime assertion states an SCR keeps a sounder energised specifically "even if the loop is reclosed" -- a normally-closed-loop-reclose-survival behaviour tied to the retired, unevidenced NC-loop/bias topology, sourced from a hobbyist tutorial site outside any permitted authority class. [Section F, third narrow correction pass] The governed EDA-LP-25 required facet (the general relationship: a triggered, latched SCR can keep current flowing through a bell/buzzer/sounder until current falls below holding current, via supply interruption or reset) is now VERIFIED via a genuine PA decision (PA-UNIT202-20260906-SCR-ALARM-EXEMPLAR-001, Ray Marston/Nuts & Volts). This does NOT cover the runtime's more specific "survives loop reclose" claim, which remains tied to the still-retired NC-loop topology -- the runtime content should be corrected to teach the general, now-evidenced relationship rather than the specific, still-unevidenced loop-reclose behaviour. The general transistor-switching and SCR-latching principles remain correctly, separately mapped to EDA-LP-10/EDA-LP-11.
